findings.title: Missing Schema.org Organization structured data on root landing page
findings.evidence: Observed at https://www.indiatimes.com/ via jsonld_schema_extractor [2026-09-13T16:09:20Z]: Root homepage contains 0 Organization or LocalBusiness JSON-LD schema blocks. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.summary: Add Organization JSON-LD markup to the homepage.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add a JSON-LD script on the homepage declaring @type 'Organization' with name, url, logo, and sameAs links to authoritative profiles.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves structured data by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.
suggested_action.fix_snippet:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Organization",
  "name": "Indiatimes",
  "url": "https://www.indiatimes.com",
  "logo": "REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_LOGO_URL",
  "description": "Indiatimes is your destination when it comes to exploring the latest in lifestyle trends, health and wellness hacks, and fashion advice. From food fads to travel tips and relationship rules, we tell you how to live your best life. Bookmark this for all the latest lifestyle content tailored just for you.",
  "email": "grievance.it@timesinternet.in",
  "sameAs": [
    "REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_WIKIPEDIA_OR_LINKEDIN_URL"
  ]
}
</script>

findings.title: Deep pages never identify the brand, leaving cold arrivals unoriented
findings.evidence: Observed at https://www.indiatimes.com/news/cm-pushkar-singh-dhami-reviews-master-plan-for-rishikul-institute-in-haridwar/articleshow/134113349.html via cold_arrival_brand_mention_check [2026-09-13T16:09:20Z]: 3 deep page(s) contain no mention of "Indiatimes" in the title or body text (e.g. https://www.indiatimes.com/news/cm-pushkar-singh-dhami-reviews-master-plan-for-rishikul-institute-in-haridwar/articleshow/134113349.html, https://www.indiatimes.com/entertainment/movies-like-kikis-delivery-service-where-to-watch-howls-moving-castle-ponyo-and-more/articleshow/134182685.html). A visitor arriving here from an AI citation, with no homepage context, cannot tell whose site they are on -- and neither can an assistant attributing the quote. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.summary: Name the brand in the header, title and footer of every page.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Include the brand name in the <title> of every page and in a persistent header or footer, so a page that is the visitor's first contact still identifies its owner.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves orientation by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

findings.title: Training-only AI crawlers are blocked; search and retrieval agents remain allowed
findings.evidence: Observed at https://indiatimes.com/robots.txt via robots_txt_parser_longest_match [2026-09-13T16:09:20Z]: robots.txt disallows root '/' for training crawlers (Meta-ExternalAgent) while leaving search-index and user-triggered agents allowed. This is a coherent licensing stance and does not prevent the brand being cited in AI answers. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.summary: No change needed; confirm this is intentional and state the policy explicitly.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: If deliberate, make it legible by adding a Content Signals Policy block or RSL licensing terms to robots.txt so the distinction between training and retrieval is machine-readable rather than inferred from which agents you named.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves crawlability by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

findings.title: No site search affordance found on any crawled page
findings.evidence: Observed at https://www.indiatimes.com via search_affordance_detection [2026-09-13T16:09:20Z]: None of the 5 crawled pages expose a search input, a search form or role="search". A visitor who arrives on the wrong page from an AI answer has no way to find the right one without returning to the assistant. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Add a site search box to the persistent header.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add a search input in the global header and expose it with role="search". Add WebSite JSON-LD with a potentialAction SearchAction so assistants can surface your search directly.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves navigation by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

findings.title: No returning-visitor or account affordance detected
findings.evidence: Observed at https://www.indiatimes.com via returning_visitor_affordance_detection [2026-09-13T16:09:20Z]: Across 5 crawled pages there is no sign-in, account, saved-items or recently-viewed affordance in the visible text. Every visitor is therefore treated as anonymous and first-time, so nothing the brand already knows about a returning visitor can shape what they are shown. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Give returning visitors a way to be recognised, and use it.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add an account or saved-state affordance appropriate to the site (sign-in, saved items, recently viewed, or a lightweight preference stored locally), then use it to surface relevant content on return rather than resetting every visitor to a cold start.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves personalization readiness by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

assessments.reason: robots.txt was fetched and its rules were applied to page and link fetches.
Initial HTML was inspected for shell signals; no browser rendering was used.
Answerability was checked against accessible on-site text and structured data only.
Only explicitly linked authority domains were inspected; external sources were not fabricated or searched.
No agent-supplied external discovery evidence was provided; no external search was performed.

proactive_recommendations.title: Mark up existing question-and-answer content with FAQPage schema
proactive_recommendations.rationale: The site already contains question-shaped content, but none of it is marked as FAQPage. FAQPage is the highest-leverage schema type for AI citation because its question/answer structure matches how retrieval systems chunk content and lift a quotable answer. The content already exists; only the markup is missing.

suggested_action.summary: Add FAQPage JSON-LD to pages that already answer common questions.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Wrap each question and its answer in FAQPage JSON-LD with mainEntity -> Question -> acceptedAnswer. Mark up the answers you already publish rather than writing new ones.

proactive_recommendations.title: State AI usage terms explicitly in robots.txt
proactive_recommendations.rationale: robots.txt names which agents may crawl but says nothing about what may be done with the content once fetched. Emerging conventions -- Cloudflare's Content Signals Policy (released CC0) and RSL licensing terms -- let a publisher separate training use from search indexing and answer generation in machine-readable form, instead of leaving that distinction to be inferred from which user agents happen to be listed.

suggested_action.summary: Add machine-readable content-usage signals to robots.txt.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add a Content Signals Policy block declaring your position on search, ai-input and ai-train separately, or publish RSL licensing terms. Keep it consistent with the agents you actually allow, or the two signals will contradict each other.

proactive_recommendations.title: Expose an agent-facing endpoint (NLWeb / MCP) built on existing structured data
proactive_recommendations.rationale: The site already publishes structured data, which is the input NLWeb uses to serve a conversational endpoint that AI agents can query directly rather than scraping HTML. Because it builds on schema.org markup, sitemaps and feeds you already maintain, it is incremental rather than a rebuild, and it moves the brand from being read by agents to being queryable by them.

suggested_action.summary: Evaluate an NLWeb instance exposing an /ask and /mcp endpoint over existing content.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Point an NLWeb instance at your existing schema.org data and sitemap, and expose /ask and /mcp. Start with the content an agent is most likely to be asked about -- catalogue, docs, pricing.

proactive_recommendations.title: Consider publishing llms.txt, with realistic expectations
proactive_recommendations.rationale: No /llms.txt is published. Be aware this is a low-evidence convention rather than an established standard: 2026 measurements find major AI crawlers almost never request the file, and Google has stated it has no effect on Search or AI Overviews. It costs very little to publish and may matter if uptake improves, but it should be treated as optionality -- not as a substitute for the structured data and third-party presence that demonstrably drive citation today.

suggested_action.summary: Optionally publish /llms.txt, after the higher-leverage items above.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: If you publish one, keep it to a short markdown index of your canonical product, docs, pricing and company pages, and keep it in sync with the site. Do not deprioritise schema work for it.
